_note: Hall of Pioneers (spec D15). Edit text here; no code change needed. DRAFT: the organizers' reviewer must verify every line before launch. 'story' is the detail-view text (up to 60 words); leave it empty to show only 'known'. 'initials' is optional and overrides the automatic initials. 'findIt' names the game where the idea appears, or null.

pioneers.name: Max Planck
pioneers.known: Proposed in 1900 that energy comes in discrete packets, which started quantum theory.

pioneers.name: Niels Bohr
pioneers.known: Model of the atom with quantized energy levels, and the principle of complementarity.

pioneers.name: Erwin Schrödinger
pioneers.known: The wave equation of quantum mechanics, and the cat thought experiment.

pioneers.name: Paul Dirac
pioneers.known: Combined quantum mechanics with special relativity, and introduced bra-ket notation.

pioneers.name: Satyendra Nath Bose
pioneers.known: Kolkata-born physicist whose work on photon statistics led to Bose-Einstein statistics; bosons are named after him.

pioneers.name: John Bell
pioneers.known: Bell's theorem (1964), which made entanglement testable.

pioneers.name: Richard Feynman
pioneers.known: Proposed computers that use quantum mechanics to simulate nature.

pioneers.name: David Deutsch
pioneers.known: Described the universal quantum computer and an early algorithm showing quantum advantage.

pioneers.name: Peter Shor
pioneers.known: Quantum algorithm for factoring integers, and the first quantum error-correcting code.

pioneers.name: Lov Grover
pioneers.known: Quantum algorithm for searching unsorted data with a quadratic speedup.

pioneers.name: Charles Bennett and Gilles Brassard
pioneers.known: BB84, the first quantum key distribution protocol.

pioneers.name: Chien-Shiung Wu
pioneers.known: Experimental physicist whose 1950 photon-pair experiment with Irving Shaknov is an early entanglement test, and whose 1957 experiment showed that parity is not conserved in weak interactions.

pioneers.name: Alain Aspect, John Clauser, and Anton Zeilinger
pioneers.known: Experiments with entangled photons that confirmed violations of Bell inequalities; shared the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics.
